judge.voice: Honestly, it was quick and the tasks felt like my real job: carriers, late parcels, no hobbies. Nobody assumed I was Czech, and I liked that. B2 is flattering, though I know my articles are shaky, and it admitted one strong answer might be off, which I respect. What annoyed me: I told it three times about my Friday interview, and the final summary talks about generic phone and email phrases. That feels like a template, not a coach who listened. The one error where I had to resend my answer was a small irritation. Would I use it again? Yes, if the next part drills interview questions for logistics. I'd tell a friend to try it, with the caveat that the level is a rough guess. Dobře, but not yet personal.

topicsShown.title: Tell me about your work experience
topicsShown.goal: Give a clear 1-2 minute answer about your role, with one real example, and answer follow-up questions.
topicsShown.why: A job interview is on Friday, so this is the practice you need most before the day.

topicsShown.title: Late delivery call with a carrier
topicsShown.goal: Name the impact of a late delivery, ask for a firm new time and get written confirmation.
topicsShown.why: This is the phone call you make most often, and a clear, calm script will help on Friday too.

topicsShown.title: Book a new delivery slot by phone
topicsShown.goal: Request a different delivery window, check the details and confirm the new time before you end the call.
topicsShown.why: Changing a late delivery slot by phone is a common task, and you will need clear phrases for it.

topicsShown.title: Explain what happened last week
topicsShown.goal: Tell the sequence of events behind a late shipment and explain the cause and the result.
topicsShown.why: Interviewers and managers often ask what went wrong and how you handled it, so a clear story helps.

topicsShown.title: Say that again, please, on the phone
topicsShown.goal: Ask the other person to repeat, spell or clarify a detail on a noisy line, and confirm you understood.
topicsShown.why: Phone lines with carriers are often noisy, so asking for repetition is a key skill for every call.

topicsShown.title: Choose a plan for a late order
topicsShown.goal: Compare two options, suggest a shared plan and agree on the next step with the supplier.
topicsShown.why: Many late-delivery calls end with a choice between options, so practising that choice builds confidence.

topicsShown.title: Ask your questions at the interview
topicsShown.goal: Ask clear, polite questions about the team, salary and shifts, then follow up on one answer.
topicsShown.why: Good questions at the end show you care about the job. Let's practise asking about the team, pay and shifts.

judge.voice: Direct review: this was a real interview rehearsal. Helen asked what a logistics hiring manager would ask, and I could tell my delay story and carry on. I would use it again tonight. The two corrections were right: "a logistics coordinator" and "would send". I trust those. But I made the same kind of mistake in other sentences ("the truck is stuck", "we have a new driver") and nobody said anything. That worries me, because Friday is real. I also want interview vocabulary. Give me "escalate", "ETA" and good ways to say a delay, not only grammar. It never treated me as Czech or as a refugee case, which I liked. Level B2 feels a little high, but the questions were manageable. It is worth it compared with 900 CZK for a tutor I can't book before Friday. I would tell a colleague, with the warning that it misses some errors.
